tr.een muur over hoe alles in elkaar zit: a wall about how everything holds everything
tr.breek een foto, en je hebt twee halve fo:
break a photograph, and you have two half photographs.
break a hologram, and every shard holds the whole image:
a little vaguer, and seen from its own angle.

tr.onder een boom liggen ronde vlekken lich:
under a tree lie round patches of light, even though the gaps between the leaves are angular.
each patch is an image of the sun: a small hole works like a lens without glass.
tr.aristoteles vroeg zich al af waarom ze r:
aristotle already wondered why they are round. marcel minnaert opened his book with them
(light and colour in the open air, utrecht 1937): measure such a patch, multiply by 108,
and you know how high the gap is.

tr.de rand weet waar de steentjes vielen: the rim knows where the pebbles fell
tr.christiaan huygens (1678): elk punt van:
christiaan huygens (1678): every point of a wave is itself a source of waves.
that is why every bit of a wave carries news of the whole.

mathias fink (paris) recorded a bang with a ring of microphones and played it back in reverse:
the sound ran back to where the bang had been. the water above really does this; it is computed.

dennis gabor thought of it in 1947. let the light from a thing collide with light that came straight on,
and catch that collision on a plate. no image appears on it: only stripes, finer than a hair.
tr.schijn er weer licht door, en het ding s:
shine light through it again, and the thing is there again. his first plate (1948, by the green light
of a mercury lamp, the laser did not exist yet) carried three names: huygens, young, fresnel.
tr.deze plaat is echt uitgerekend. houd er:
this plate is really computed. hold on to one shard of it: the whole word stays, only vaguer.
(it is there twice, upright and as a mirror image: that is what a hologram does.)
tr.geen enkele streep weet iets van het woo: no single stripe knows anything of the word. together they are the word.

tr.snijd haar door, en je hebt er twee: cut her in two, and you have two
tr.een platworm uit de sloot, een centimete:
a flatworm from the ditch, a centimetre long. cut her in half: the head piece makes a new tail,
the tail piece a new head, with eyes and a brain in it.
tr.thomas hunt morgan (1898): zelfs een stu:
thomas hunt morgan (1898): even a piece of 1/279 grows back into a whole worm.
hans driesch (1891) shook the first two cells of a sea urchin apart. he expected two half
larvae, and got two whole ones. that is also how identical twins begin.
tr.waar staat hoe een hele worm eruitziet?:
where is it written what a whole worm looks like? not only in the genes. michael levin changed the electrical
pattern across a piece of worm: it grew two heads, and kept doing so, cut after cut.
every part knows what the whole looks like.

a coast: the shorter your ruler,
the longer it gets
tr.elk veertje van een varen is zelf een kl:
every leaflet of a fern is itself a small fern. and so is every leaflet of that one.
benoît mandelbrot gave it a name in 1975: fractal.
tr.een hologram bevat het geheel in elk dee:
a hologram contains the whole in every part. a fern repeats the whole in every part:
two ways in which the large sits inside the small. in a real fern it stops after a few steps; here never.
tr.wie groeit door te vertakken, lijkt in h: whatever grows by branching looks, in the small, like itself in the large.

and all fields interwoven

tr.karl lashley leerde ratten een doolhof,:
karl lashley taught rats a maze, and then cut away a different piece of their cortex each time.
no single piece held the memory. the more he cut away, the vaguer it became: never gone at once (1950).
tr.karl pribram dacht daarom aan een hologr:
that made karl pribram think of a hologram. it is not that literal: a memory lives in a scattered
group of cells. but scattered it is.
tr.john hopfield bouwde in 1982 een net waa:
in 1982 john hopfield built a net in which every memory sits in all the wires at once (nobel prize 2024).
this net holds the eight other walls: 400 points, 79,800 wires, and nowhere a picture.
give a part, and the whole comes up.
tr.(wie deze wand maakte is zelf zo’n net:: (whoever made this wall is such a net too: what i know is written nowhere in one place. fable)

this looks like none of the eight

tr.in elke druppel de hele ochtend: in every drop the whole morning
tr.in de hemel van indra hangt een net, in:
in the heaven of indra hangs a net, endless in every direction. in every knot a jewel,
and in every jewel all the other jewels are mirrored, with their reflections too.
tr.(avatamsaka-soetra, ruim vijftienhonderd:
(avatamsaka sutra, more than fifteen hundred years old.) the monk fazang showed it to empress wu,
around the year 700: ten mirrors around one lamp. leibniz (1714): each thing is a living mirror of the universe,
from its own angle. william blake: to see a world in a grain of sand.
tr.en het is ook gewoon waar: een dauwdrupp: and it is also simply true: a dewdrop is a lens. the whole landscape stands in it, upside down.

tr.dertien bloemen, en in elke bloem de hel: thirteen flowers, and in every flower the whole tree
tr.de kabbala tekent het bewustzijn als een:
the kabbalah draws consciousness as a tree of spheres. in every sphere the whole tree sits once more,
wrote the kabbalists of safed in the sixteenth century: and in that again, without end.
tr.frank zweers legde de boom in de levensb:
frank zweers laid the tree in the flower of life, with thirteen spheres: the ten familiar ones, the hidden sphere of knowledge,
and at the bottom the serpent and the fruit. three centres: head, heart and belly. a sphere that lives, turns, and takes its neighbours along.
(levensboom, holographic puzzle of existence, 2020)
tr.dit is geen natuurkunde. het is een oude: this is not physics. it is an old map of the same suspicion: that the whole returns in every part.
tr.dezelfde sfeer licht op in elke kleine b: the same sphere lights up in every small tree

tr.een druppel inkt in stroperige glycerine:
a drop of ink in syrupy glycerine, between two glass cylinders. turn the inner one: the drop stretches
into a thread, and disappears. turn exactly back: there it is again.
tr.de natuurkundige david bohm zag deze pro:
the physicist david bohm saw this experiment on television, and thought: perhaps the whole world is put together like this.
what we see is the unfolded. beneath it lies an order in which everything is folded into everything
(wholeness and the implicate order, 1980).
tr.de proef is gewone natuurkunde: stroop m: the experiment is ordinary physics: syrup does not mix, it shears. bohm’s thought is a proposal, beautiful and unproven.
tr.de druppel was nooit weg. ze zat in het: the drop was never gone. it was folded into the whole.

tr.david bohm vertelde het zo: twee camera’:
david bohm told it like this: two cameras film one aquarium, from the front and from the side.
whoever knows only the two screens sees two fish that sense each other flawlessly.
tr.zo gedragen twee verstrengelde deeltjes:
this is how two entangled particles behave: measure one, and you know the other, however far apart they are.
in 1964 john bell worked out how to check whether they had agreed on it beforehand. alain aspect did the experiment (1982):
not agreed. in delft (2015) once more, watertight, with two diamonds 1.3 kilometres apart.
tr.je kunt er geen bericht mee sturen. en w: you cannot send a message with it. and what it means, physicists do not agree on.
tr.bohm zei: het zijn geen twee dingen. het: bohm said: they are not two things. it is one thing, seen from two sides.
tr.twee vissen. draait de ene, dan draait d: two fish. when one turns, the other turns too. are they signalling each other?

tr.alles wat erin valt, staat op zijn huid: everything that falls in is written on its skin
tr.gooi iets in een zwart gat, en je bent h:
throw something into a black hole, and you have lost it. but what fell in still counts: the hole grows,
and it is not its volume but its surface that keeps the score (jacob bekenstein, 1972; stephen hawking, 1974).
tr.een zwart gat is precies zo groot als wa:
a black hole is exactly as big as what it knows. no space of that size can hold more information:
a 1 followed by 69 zeros in bits per square metre of edge. so whatever can happen in a space fits on its wall.
tr.gerard ’t hooft (utrecht, 1993) trok de:
gerard ’t hooft (utrecht, 1993) drew the conclusion: perhaps the whole world can be described on a surface,
the way a hologram keeps a space on a plate. leonard susskind gave it its name: the holographic principle.
tr.hawking dacht lang dat het gat alles voo:
for a long time hawking thought the hole erased everything for good. in 2004 he conceded:
it radiates everything out again, scrambled beyond recognition, but not gone.
tr.het gat vergeet niets. het bewaart het o: the hole forgets nothing. it keeps it on its skin.
tr.genoeg voor nu: kijk hoe het langzaam we: enough for now: watch it slowly radiate it out again

tr.een wereld die op haar eigen omtrek past: a world that fits on its own rim
tr.juan maldacena vond in 1997 een wereld w:
in 1997 juan maldacena found a world in which it holds exactly: everything that happens inside,
gravity and all, is also written on the edge, without gravity. two stories, one world.
tr.zo’n wereld is krom, zoals deze schijf::
such a world is curved, like this disc: all the pentagons here are the same size, and towards the edge more and more of them fit.
m.c. escher already drew it in 1958, in his circle limits.
tr.wijs een punt aan: uit dat stuk van de r:
point at a spot: it can be read back from that stretch of the edge. the deeper the point, the wider it is smeared
across the edge. mark van raamsdonk (2010): cut the connectedness on the edge, and the space inside
falls apart. perhaps space is woven from connectedness.
tr.ons eigen heelal is niet zo’n schijf. of: our own universe is not such a disc. whether it is a hologram too, nobody knows. the suspicion will not go away.
tr.wat diep vanbinnen ligt, staat breed ove: what lies deep inside is written wide across the edge.

tr.of het heelal een hologram is, weet niem: whether the universe is a hologram, nobody knows. but this much is certain:
tr.in je oog komt nu het licht van alles om:
in your eye the light of everything around you is now coming together.
in almost every cell of your body lies the whole plan.
in your memory lives everyone you have known.
the iron in your blood was forged in stars.
you are not a loose piece of the world.
tr.je bent de wereld, vanuit één hoek gezie: you are the world, seen from one angle.
tr.en ergens hangt een druppel dauw aan een: and somewhere a drop of dew hangs on a web, with the whole morning in it.
